name: Device Automation
summary: Atlas for IoT automation: a device Worker Type that drives outputs (GPIO, PWM, buses, e-paper displays) and turns physical inputs into messages, from a Raspberry Pi hosting the server down to a microcontroller speaking the job protocol, with safe states enforced on the device.
next_action: Review the device core (IOT1 increment 1) with the programme registration; then IOT1 increment 2: the <atlas:deviceConnector> compiler element and reserved job type, the device Worker kind in the server, and atlas worker --connector device with a mock chip, so a model drives a relay end to end.

slices.title: Decision and threat model
slices.note: The owner accepted option 4 of the Device Workers record on 2026-11-05: a device Worker Type defined as a contract over the existing job protocol, MQTT later. Open: the threat model for physically exposed device credentials, which gates IOT2.

slices.title: Linux outputs: digital.write, digital.read, pulse
slices.note: First, because every later slice configures a device Worker and this slice creates it. Increment 1 on branch claude/focused-gauss-i29wni: connector/device and its catalog — named outputs with safe state, on-duration watchdog and pulse deduplication by job key, the GPIO v2 character-device ABI in pure Go with its layout pinned by test, a FakeChip; 98.4% statement coverage; the opt-in hardware test passed on the reference Pi Zero 2 W (gpiochip0 line 26) on 2026-11-05. Next increments: compiler element and reserved job type, server Worker kind and atlas worker --connector device; then Modeler, setup doc and handbook. Runs with today's worker token scope.

slices.title: Inputs to messages and the device token scope
slices.note: Edges and debounce on the device, POST /api/v1/messages with timeToLiveMs and a messageId of device id, boot id and counter; a device scope reaching the job protocol and only the message names the Worker's inputs declare.

slices.title: E-paper display.show
slices.note: One reference panel on a Pi Zero: declarative layout resolved on lease, rasterised on the device with an Umlaut-capable font, content hash, refresh interval, stale marker as the display's safe state; SPI implemented with the driver, not exposed to models.

slices.title: PWM, I2C and 1-Wire
slices.note: pwm.set, i2c.read/i2c.write against configured bus devices, onewire.read (e.g. DS18B20).

slices.title: Microcontroller client and protocol conformance suite
slices.note: MicroPython reference client for a Pico 2 W; a conformance suite any client can be run against. Settles the open question on TLS long-poll within the microcontroller's RAM and how that tier renders text.

slices.title: Edge server on a Raspberry Pi
slices.note: Measured sizing of atlas serve and atlas worker on Pi Zero W, Zero 2 W and Pi 5; an example application; the handbook card in both languages.

slices.title: Coupling an edge Atlas with a central Atlas
slices.note: Needs its own ADR: two engines with their own logs have no cross-engine process today. Decide what crosses (messages, jobs, both), in which direction, and what each side may do while the other is unreachable.

slices.title: People acting through a device
slices.note: A display with a button is an approval terminal nobody logged into. Decide with the Identity-aware Execution programme who a button press is attributed to before a device may complete human work.

slices.title: MQTT bridge for off-the-shelf devices
slices.note: Own ADR. Broker QoS acknowledges delivery to the broker, not the effect; a request/response pattern is needed before a job may complete on it.
